newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says would raise rates if necessary.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says would raise rates if necessary.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday he was prepared to raise interest rates if it was necessary to counter inflation.
"I will do whatever is necessary but at the moment there are a lack of inflationary pressures," he told a news conference.
"As soon as they show signs of rising I will act."
He added that his budget had produced a modest fiscal tightening and he did not think policy was too loose at the moment.
"I leave myself all the room for manoeuvre I require to meet the inflation target," Clarke said.
The chancellor rejected suggestions that his budget had been overly cautious in an attempt to meet the Maastricht debt and deficit criteria.
"I have not drawn up the budget to aim at the Maastricht criteria," he said, adding that it was a coincidence that the budget had forecast that Britain would meet the criteria.
Responding to queries about spending forecasts factoring in a fall in unemployment, Clarke said:
"It's a reasonable assumption that there will be some drop (in unemployment)."
